bib.title: VIOLET: End-to-End Video-Language Transformers with Masked Visual-token Modeling

read.skipped: References skimmed only; figures 6-9 are qualitative images.

question: Does explicit temporal modelling with a video transformer plus a discrete-token masked visual pre-training task improve end-to-end video-language models over mean-pooled or concatenated frame features?
hypothesis: Mean pooling or concatenation of sparse frame features loses temporal information; a Video Swin encoder and Masked Visual-token Modeling (MVM) will improve video-language tasks.
contributions: VIOLET, a fully end-to-end video-language transformer modelling spatial-temporal dynamics
Masked Visual-token Modeling, recovering masked patches in a discrete visual token space
State of the art on 4 text-to-video retrieval and 5 out of 8 video question answering tasks
Ablations showing the need for temporal video modelling and the effect of MVM across pre-training settings

method.summary: VIOLET feeds T sparsely sampled frames to a Video Swin Transformer, concatenates the per-frame features with BERT word embeddings and fuses them in a cross-modal BERT transformer. Pre-training uses VTM, MLM and the new MVM (targets from DALL-E's dVAE) with blockwise and attended masking, then fine-tunes end to end per task.
method.task: video-language pre-training; text-to-video retrieval and video question answering

datasets.name: YT-Temporal-180M
datasets.size: 6M YouTube videos, 180M video-subtitle pairs (every 4 consecutive segments, avg segment 9.29 s)
datasets.preprocessing: ASR text concatenated for each middle frame as text input

datasets.name: MSRVTT
datasets.split: train on 9K train+val, evaluate on 1K-A test

datasets.name: DiDeMo
datasets.preprocessing: all sentences of a video concatenated into a paragraph

datasets.name: TGIF-QA (Action, Transition, Frame), MSRVTT-MC/QA, MSVD-QA, LSMDC-MC/FiB
datasets.size: MSRVTT-QA 243K questions over 10K videos; MSVD-QA 47K questions over 2K videos
datasets.preprocessing: open-ended QA as classification over most common answers: 1,540 (TGIF-Frame), 1,500 (MSRVTT-QA), 1,000 (MSVD-QA), 908 (LSMDC-FiB); multiple choice 5 options

datasets.name: VCR
datasets.preprocessing: colored highlights on referenced entities as in MERLOT

models.name: VIOLET
models.architecture: Video Swin Transformer + Language Embedder + Cross-modal Transformer (BERT-Base)
models.init_from: VideoSwin-Base (Kinetics-400); BERT-Base for language embedder and cross-modal transformer

models.name: Mean / Concat ablations
models.architecture: ResNet-50 per-frame features, mean-pooled or concatenated, fed to cross-modal transformer

models.name: ClipBERT, Frozen, Clip4Clip, MERLOT, JustAsk, etc.

training.objective: VTM + MLM + MVM (cross-entropy over dVAE visual tokens for masked patches; MLM mask 15% with 80/10/10 BERT scheme; VTM binary match with in-batch negative text). Blockwise masking until >15% patches masked, attended masking picks top 15% most-attended tokens. Fine-tuning: binary match for retrieval, cross-entropy for QA
training.lr: 2e-5 pre-training; 1.2e-5 initial fine-tuning (task-specific learning rates by validation)
training.batch_size: fine-tuning: 56 (MSRVTT, YouCook2, LSMDC retrieval), 48 (DiDeMo, TGIF-Frame, MSRVTT-MC/QA, VCR), 80 (MSVD-QA, LSMDC-MC/FiB); pre-training batch size not stated
training.epochs: pre-training 5 epochs YT-Temporal then 5 epochs WebVid+CC; fine-tuning 20 epochs (MSRVTT, DiDeMo, TGIF-Frame, MSRVTT QA/MC, VCR) or 40 (YouCook2, LSMDC, MSVD-QA, LSMDC-MC/FiB)
training.hardware: fine-tuning: Microsoft Azure, 8 Nvidia V100 (32GB); pre-training GPU type V100
training.compute: 2,240 GPU hours on V100 for pre-training (text also says 2K)

other.curriculum: YT-Temporal with ASR first, then WebVid+CC with alt-text

inference.samples: single run per setting; no seeds or variance reported
inference.retrieval: each text-video pair scored by FC on [CLS]; one fused forward pass per pair (cross-encoder, no embedding index); zero-shot uses pre-trained FC_VTM

eval.protocol: standard splits; learning rate and epochs chosen on validation; no seeds or significance tests stated

limits: No frame-count ablation: T is fixed at 4 (pre-training) and 5 (downstream).
Retrieval is a per-pair cross-encoder; retrieval cost over a corpus is not discussed.
Mean/Concat ablation baselines use ResNet-50 while VT uses Video Swin, so encoder and temporal modelling are confounded.
No seeds, variance or significance tests; no pre-training batch size, schedule or warmup.
Authors concede: densely sampled full-length videos (e.g. TGIF-Count) and audio are future work; larger resolution and longer pre-training would help.
Trails Clip4Clip (CLIP pre-trained on 400M pairs) and MERLOT on some tasks.

terms.definition: feed a handful of sparsely sampled frames to a 2D CNN, then mean-pool or concatenate to obtain the video representation
recover the discrete dVAE visual tokens of masked video patches

lineage.note: sparse sampling and mean pooling that VIOLET replaces with temporal modelling
MVM takes inspiration, extended to video
